Madam President, we support the European Parliament's resolution on.

The situation of human rights in Cuba. the statement made by Senegal in its capacity as chair of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People. We also support those statements that will be made by Uganda on behalf of NAM and Venezuela on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defence of the United Nations Charter. Since the last open debate on this topic, The United States military attacks against the Islamic Republic of Iran have broadened the conflict and plunged the region into a dangerous escalation of tensions. We strongly condemn the use of force. It constitutes a flagrant violation of the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and international law. We unequivocally reaffirm the principle of respect for national sovereignty and the territorial integrity of all nations in the region, including the Arab Gulf states, along with the call to uphold the principles of good neighborliness, restraint and dialogue at this difficult time. Madam President, the continued and illegal Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory and other occupied Arab territories, as well as the disproportionate and sustained use of force and the lack of accountability for serious violations of international law, all of this with the political, military, financial and diplomatic backing of the United States, continues to fuel a dangerous spiral of violence with wholesale repercussions for regional and international peace and security. Cuba condemns in the very strongest terms the continuation of these illegal Israeli practices. They continue to claim the lives of Palestinian civilians, including women and children. It is equally unacceptable to see the use of starvation as a method of warfare, the deliberate destruction of civilian infrastructure essential to the population's survival, and the obstacles imposed on humanitarian assistance. Israel's actions constitute a flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter and of international humanitarian law. Moreover, they breach numerous resolutions of the Security Council as well as those of the General Assembly, resolutions which reaffirm the inalienable right of the Palestinian people to self-determination. It will not be possible to achieve a just and lasting peace in the Middle East without a comprehensive and definitive solution being found to the Palestinian question, a solution that puts an end to the genocide against this people. Palestine must be admitted without delay as a fully-fledged member state of the United Nations. It is urgent that the Palestinian people be able to exercise their inalienable right to an independent and sovereign state within the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, based on the two-state solution. Likewise, the right of return for refugees must be guaranteed. We decry the attacks waged by the Zionist regime of Israel in southern Lebanon. These actions constitute a flagrant violation of international law and of international humanitarian law against a sovereign state. Israel must cease its aggression against Lebanese territory and respect Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity. These are prerequisites for peace and stability in the Middle East. We once again call for Israel's total and unconditional withdrawal from the Syrian Golan, a territory recognized as an integral part of Syria, and from all occupied Arab territories. President, the dangerous escalation of the conflict in the Middle East confirms that coercion and the aberrant doctrine that seeks to impose peace through force only generates instability and deepens the suffering of peoples. We have warned time and time again of the danger of these practices, the danger they pose to Latin American Latin America and the Caribbean. Cuba is a peaceful country that poses no threat whatsoever to the United States or to any other nation. We suffer the consequences of a policy of economic strangulation rooted in a blockade which was imposed 70 years ago by the United States. It includes a severe energy blockade whose effects are equivalent to a naval blockade. This act of war and of genocide subjects the Cuban people to conditions that threaten their integrity and their very existence. Moreover, it constitutes a cruel and indiscriminate form of collective punishment. Moreover, we see other criminal extraterritorial measures and recurring threats of military aggression from the highest levels of the US government. These are issued with total impunity in flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter, international law and the principles of the Proclamation of Latin America and the Caribbean as a Zone of Peace. Such threats are reported in public sources where dangerous options and preparations for war are described. The Security Council bears the primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. As such, it should act with resolve and in strict accordance with its mandate to prevent a military attack by the United States against Cuba. Such an attack would have incalculable consequences not only for both countries but also for the entire hemisphere and for international peace and security. Our collective aspiration must be that of an international order free of blockades, unilateral coercive measures, hegemony and attempts at domination. Ours must be an international, just international order that guarantees peace and development for all peoples. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Cuba for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Turkey.

Thank you, Madam President. I also thank Deputy Special Coordinator Alakbarov for his comprehensive presentation. Madam President, the realization of the two-state solution is indispensable to the peace, security, and stability of the wider Middle East. The international community has affirmed this unequivocally, most recently at the High-Level International Conference for the Peaceful Settlement of the Question of Palestine and the Implementation of the Two-State Solution. It is likewise a central pillar of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict, which underscores Palestinian self-determination and statehood and rejects annexation. Yet for too long, expressions of concern have outpaced concrete action, while developments on the ground have moved steadily away from peace. The Palestinian people are entitled to a full and lasting peace rather than intermittent conflict. The comprehensive plan and the Security Council Resolution 2803 should therefore serve as our guiding framework. The successful implementation of the comprehensive plan is the only viable way to stabilize Gaza. Along with this, the sustainable peace and stability in Gaza rests on four indispensable elements. First, the full, sustained, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza must be ensured. UNRWA is an indispensable partner in this regard. Second, a durable ceasefire cannot coexist with continued occupation. Sustainable peace requires full withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. Third, reconstruction efforts must commence immediately, enabling Gazans to rebuild their homes, their communities, and their future. Fourth, and most fundamentally, a credible and irreversible pathway toward the two-state solution must be advanced. Anything less than the establishment of an independent, sovereign, and contiguous state of Palestine based on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital will postpone the next crisis rather than resolve this one. Madam President, My delegation feels obliged to respond to the allegations directed at my country, the official name of which is Turkey. These words carry limited weight coming from a delegation with one of the worst records of compliance with international law. Turkey is in the view that a lasting settlement requires engagement with all parties involved in the conflict, whose continued participation remains essential to the implementation of the comprehensive plan. Ignoring this reality will not help stabilization in Palestine. The mediation efforts of Turkey, United States, Qatar, and Egypt brought an end to hostilities in Gaza. These efforts must now be followed by sustained political action. Madam President, Israel's actions in the occupied West Bank are converting the threat of annexation into a de facto reality. Similarly, Israel's aggression on Lebanon and Syria remains a matter of serious concern. Turkey condemns the rising settler violence in the occupied Palestinian territories. The killing of four Palestinians on July 24th is a direct consequence of the persistent impunity granted to Israel. We also condemn in the strongest terms the storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israeli officials. We reject these acts that violate the historical and legal status of the holy sites in Jerusalem and desecrate their religious prominence. In conclusion, Madam President, we renew our call on this council to ensure the full implementation of the ceasefire and the comprehensive plan. take concrete steps to halt settlement expansion, forced civil displacement, and other unlawful practices in the occupied Palestinian territories, and ensure accountability for the crimes committed. We urge the international community to move beyond rhetoric and take concrete steps to secure a just peace for all peoples of the region. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Turkey for the statement, and I'll give the floor to the representative of Morocco.

Thank you, Madam President. Thank you, Madam President. I would like to thank you for holding this open debate. We commend the wise leadership of the DRC. I thank the representative of Morocco for this statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Austria. Austria.

Thank you, Madam President. The situation in the wider Middle East remains dangerously fragile, with many violent incidents despite much-welcome ceasefire agreements. At the outset, we call upon all actors to prioritise diplomatic solutions, to exercise restraint and to refrain from further violence. We welcome all efforts to find diplomatic solutions, including by Oman, Pakistan, many others, including, of course, the parties themselves, as we urgently need de-escalation as well as the resumption of free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. As all those situations are linked, allow me to focus on three. First, On the Palestinian question, Austria supports and welcomes the effort to implement the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803, which remains a challenging task. While important progress has been made, we call for full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access into and throughout Gaza and for safe working conditions for all humanitarian agencies, including UNRWA. We reiterate that Hamas cannot have a future in Gaza and that it and all other non-state armed groups must be disarmed. We regard the swift deployment of the international stabilization force to Gaza as an important step in creating the conditions for stability and recovery. At the same time, humanitarian assistance and interim arrangements do not replace a sustainable political solution. Peace will only be achieved through a negotiated two-state solution based on international law in which two states, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security. Austria has embraced the New York Declaration and is therefore particularly concerned by the continued expansion of settlements in the West Bank, annexation plans, as well as by ongoing settler violence. Second, on Syria. As discussed in a recent ARYA meeting, Austria supports the peaceful transition towards a stable, inclusive political system in Syria. Respect for human rights and the protection of all ethnic and religious groups, as well as women's rights, are of utmost importance. We welcome the recent inaugural sessions of both the People's Assembly and the Constitutional Court as positive steps. On the economic front, we see steady progress towards recovery and reconstruction. We welcome the lifting of most sanctions as well as the recent announcement by the US president to delist Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism. Austria stands ready to work together with the Syrian government towards rebuilding the country. The population of Syria needs economic perspectives, including for their safe return. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected by all actors in the region. Third on Lebanon, we welcome the Lebanese government's decision to declare Hezbollah's military activities illegal. The trilateral framework agreement of 26 June marks a significant outcome of the direct diplomatic engagements between Israel and Lebanon facilitated by the US. We welcome that the two countries are engaged in efforts to reestablish Lebanese sovereignty in southern Lebanon. As a troop contributing country to UNIFIL, Austria urges all parties to respect UNIFIL's mandate and to guarantee the safety and security of our peacekeepers. We call on the Council to ensure a transparent, comprehensive and timely planning regarding UNIFIL's drawdown, as well as regarding a suitable follow-up setting with clear involvement of the United Nations President. Let me close by reiterating that Austria stands ready to support all efforts of de-escalation through diplomacy, dialogue and the respect for international law. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Austria for the statement. I now give the floor to Mr. Quentin Wailer, delegation of the European Union to the United Nations.

Thank you, Madam President. I have the honour to speak on behalf of the European Union and its Member States. The candidate countries, Montenegro, the Republic of Moldova and Bosnia and Herzegovina, align themselves with this statement, and the full statement will be available online. The European Union expresses grave concern about the humanitarian situation in Gaza. It calls on Israel to allow full, immediate, safe and needed access and sustained distribution of humanitarian assistance at scale into and throughout Gaza, including via the Cyprus maritime corridor, and to enable the UN's agencies, including UNRWA, and humanitarian organizations to work independently and impartially. It also calls on Israel to reopen Gaza border crossings, as well as the medical corridor between Gaza and the West Bank, allow access for international media, and reverse its decision regarding the NGO registration law. European Union recalls the need to always ensure the protection of civilians, including humanitarian workers, as well as civilian infrastructure. The European Union expresses its concern about the lack of progress in the implementation of the ceasefire and all other provisions of Security Council Resolution 2803 and reiterates its call to all actors to fully implement them. We call for the permanent disarmament of Hamas and other non-state armed groups. the full withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip and the deployment of the temporary international stabilisation force. The EU will continue contributing to the implementation of this comprehensive plan in accordance with resolution 2003, including through our EU Border Assistance Mission for the Rafah crossing and the EU Police Mission for the Palestinian. The European Union will also continue to support the Palestinian Authority and its reform agenda, including the holding of elections, so that it can securely and effectively take back control of Gaza. We call again on Israel to urgently release all withheld clearance revenues and extend the corresponding banking services between Israeli and Palestinian banks. In this regard, we thank all partners who joined us at the Palestine donor group in Brussels and look forward to build on this successful meeting. The European Union expresses great concern about the deteriorating situation in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. reiterating its condemnation of the expansion of illegal settlements and settler violence. It urges the government of Israel to reverse the expansion of settlements, including in the E1 area, to abide by its obligations under international law, and to protect the Palestinian population of the occupied territories, as well as to ensure the preservation of and respect for the status quo of Jerusalem's holy sites. The European Union is looking into possible further measures against actions undermining the two-state solution. The EU is fully committed to a comprehensive, just and lasting peace based on a two-state solution in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions. The New York Declaration provides a political framework to guide these efforts. The meetings of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of a Two-State Solution demonstrate our commitment and underline the necessity to link the implementation of the Gaza peace plan and the two-state solution agenda. President, the EU deplores the resumption of hostilities between the US and Iran and the ensuing loss of life and condemns Iran's actions disrupting freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as its indiscriminate strikes on neighboring countries. We express our full solidarity with the countries affected. Recent threats by Houthis to impose a maritime blockade on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia constitute a dangerous escalation. The attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea are unacceptable, illegal, and further inflame an already volatile situation in the region. It is crucial that all actors across the region implement Security Council Resolution 2817 and refrain from actions that endanger the prospect of a negotiated solution. We commend Pakistan, Qatar, and other regional partners for the mediation efforts. And we stand ready to support future negotiations through our economic leverage, sanctions framework, nuclear expertise, maritime security engagement, direct channels with Iran, and deep partnership with the Gulf and other regional countries. Freedom of navigation and safe transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz must remain unconditional, unrestricted, and fully consistent with international law, as reflected in UNCLOS. We are engaging with Gulf and other regional partners on the day after. Based on our experience in Europe in establishing cooperation mechanisms, we welcome regional initiatives and stand ready to support and contribute to a comprehensive long-term regional solution. The EU also welcomes the framework agreement signed by Lebanon and Israel in Washington. We urge all actors to adhere to the agreement and to implement their commitments, including through the newly established trilateral military coordination group. We call for a permanent end to hostilities and full respect of international law, including international humanitarian law, and reiterate that any lasting solution must be in accordance with the implementation of resolution 1701. We call on Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanon and on Hezbollah to fully disarm in order to ensure state monopoly of arms across the whole territory. The EU stands ready to support the implementation of the framework agreement and further enhance its support for the Lebanese armed forces and the internal security forces, including through a possible EU mission. The EU recalls the importance of a continued UN presence in Lebanon and in a post UNIFIL context, it reaffirms the EU's readiness to contribute in that regard in 2027. Finally, Madam President, let me turn to Syria. The European Union remains committed to supporting a peaceful, inclusive transition in Syria that enables the participation of all Syrians without distinction and upholds their human rights without discrimination on any ground. The recent formation of the People's Assembly in Syria marks another welcome step in the country's political transition. The EU stands ready to engage with the Assembly, both to support capacity building and good governance and to work together towards achieving common goals. In this regard, the EU encourages the strengthening of cooperation between the Syrian transitional government with all UN bodies. For the transition to succeed, Syria must remain insulated from regional hostilities. The EU urges all external actors to fully respect Syria's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity in accordance with international law. And the EU calls on Israel to respect the demilitarized buffer zone and to uphold the terms of the 1974 disengagement of forces agreement.
Thank you, Mr. Vella, for your statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Mexico.

Madam President, we are meeting once again at a time in which the region of the Middle East continues to suffer on multiple fronts and it continues to be beset by growing tensions. Firstly, The freedom of navigation remains under threat, whether this be as a result of the Houthi attacks against commercial vessels in the Red Sea, or as a result of the escalation around the Strait of Hormuz, with all the economic and humanitarian implications arising therefrom. It is vital that this Council, foster the resumption of dialogue between the parties and that it helps to ensure compliance with the provisions contained in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, this in order to move towards a permanent ceasefire. It is equally imperative to guarantee the protection of civilians in theatres of conflict in accordance with international humanitarian law. We reiterate our support for the decision recently adopted by the International Maritime Organization. That decision reaffirms that the right of transit passage through the straits used for international navigation must not be threatened, denied or suspended. The decision also reaffirms the importance of ensuring that agreements between coastal states guarantee free and safe passage of all vessels through the international traffic separation scheme. Turning now to the situation between Israel and Palestine, Mexico notes the progress that has been made in terms of transferring governance to a national committee for the administration of Gaza. in coordination with the Palestinian Authority. We take note of the dissolution of the Emergency Government Committee in Gaza as a step towards a unified Palestinian government. However, the continuation and expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank, including through the E1 project, has grave consequences for the territorial contiguity of the Palestinian state. Gaza must not be annexed and this same principle must also apply to the West Bank. On the 20th of April, the UN, the World Bank and the European Union published a final assessment of damage in Gaza. That report lays bare a devastating reality. $71.4 billion will be required to meet reconstruction needs following the destruction wrought and the damage done to around 372,000 homes. Moreover, there are the effects of an economic shrinking to the tune of 84%. It is vital to move towards the reconstruction of Gaza. The bitter suffering of the Palestinian people must be brought to an end. As one of the co-chairs of the working groups of the International Conference for the Two-State Solution, Mexico here wishes to insist on the vital need to promote narratives of peace, narratives which bring about deeply rooted changes to both Israeli and Palestinian societies. For any political or security solution to be sustainable, what we need to see is a transformation, one that prioritizes peaceful coexistence, the reciprocal recognition and acknowledgement of the history of these territories and above all a transformation which moves beyond hatred and violence. Finally we also wish to welcome the appointment of Mr. Jean Arnault as UN Special Coordinator for Lebanon. We hope that the new round of direct negotiations between Israel and Lebanon will continue to bring about progress in terms of the implementation of the framework agreement reached last June, in particular the implementation of the roadmap for the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from areas in the south of Lebanon, as well as the disarmament of armed groups, the deployment of the Lebanese army in evacuated territories and the consolidation of the ceasefire. The international community and the United Nations must support any and all initiative or diplomatic effort designed to ensure that parties involved engage in negotiations in good faith to achieve a permanent ceasefire and one which leads to lasting stability. The United Nations Charter in its sixth chapter provides us with tangible options to ensure the peaceful settlement of disputes. I thank you.
I thank the representative from Mexico for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of India.

Madam President, we need to focus on the Strait of Hormuz, but also we need to focus on the tragic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We must fully support efforts by fully implementing Security Council resolutions including resolution 2803 India remains firmly committed to the efforts that impact in a positive way the lives of Palestinian civilians the humanitarian assistance provided by India to Palestine is about is valued at over 400 million US dollars this assistance comes in various forms we have provided humanitarian assistance development assistance we have also assisted UNRWA we have provided other forms of assistance as well India is one of the main donors to UNRWA We believe that this is the UN agency that will help distribute the assistance that we will deliver. During the Palestine donor group in Brussels, India announced that it is committed to build a specialized hospital and a center prosthetics as well as a vocational training centre in Palestine. On Lebanon, The blue helmets serve in challenging circumstances. UNIFIL peacekeepers pursue UN Security Council mandates and therefore must never become targets. They serve the cause of international peace and security. India has strongly condemned all attacks on UNIFIL peacekeepers. Their safety and security are a priority. The sanctity and inviolability of UN premises must be fully respected. Further, it's important to be ready for a post UNIFIL scenario. And in this context, the Lebanese armed forces must receive requisite support and assistance. The principles of sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic must remain central to all efforts. We also reiterate our support to ongoing efforts in finding long-term solutions. On Yemen, India reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Republic of Yemen and rejection of any interference in its internal affairs. We further condemn attacks by Houthis on maritime navigation. The protection of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and the southern Red Sea is a shared international responsibility and is a global interest. Madam President, the people of the Middle East need normalcy and lasting peace. As a member state guided by our civilizational doctrine of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, or the whole world is one family, India is committed to global wellbeing and a more secure, stable and prosperous world. India will continue to be driven by this approach. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the representative of India for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Norway.

Thank you, Madam President. Let me start by expressing Norway's deep concern over the current instability in the Middle East. Recent developments have once again demonstrated how quickly tensions can escalate. We urge all parties to exercise maximum restraint, to respect international law, and to prioritise dialogue over confrontation. In the context of rising regional tension, we cannot forget the situation in Palestine. Despite the ceasefire in Gaza, civilians are still being killed. The humanitarian situation remains desperate. Far too little medicine, essential goods and emergency aid is reaching an already severely affected civilian population. Despite improvements since the ceasefire, acute food insecurity remains widespread.

Furthermore,

Israel has voiced ambitions to control up to 70% of Gaza and an earthen barrier to enhance the division of Gaza is being constructed. This underlines the importance of moving forward with the implementation of the 20-point plan and Security Council Resolution 2803. Norway reiterates that international humanitarian law must be respected by all parties Humanitarian assistance must reach those in need safely, rapidly and without obstruction. The situation in the West Bank is equally concerning. Military operations, continued settlement expansion, extreme levels of settler violence, demolitions and displacements, undermine trust and threaten prospects for lasting peace. Such developments are in breach of international law and further erode the foundations for the two-state solution. President, the Palestinian Authority's worsening fiscal crisis, caused in large part by the continued withholding of revenues that belong to Palestine, as well as other economic restrictions, are bringing essential public services to the brink of collapse. We call on Israel to urgently release revenues that rightfully belong to the Palestinian people. In this context, we cannot ignore Israel's extensive use of administrative detention without formal charge. Thousands of Palestinians are being detained in Israeli prisons without charge or trial. Human rights organizations describe prison conditions for Palestinians as severe and life-threatening, citing inadequate food, denial of medical care, and abuse. We urge Israel to uphold its human rights obligations towards detainees under international law, including by granting the IC ORC immediate access to all detention facilities, as stipulated in the recent Israeli Supreme Court ruling. President, we need renewed efforts to ensure Palestinian institutions are strengthened, concrete and timely recovery and reconstruction, respect for international law and accountability. Norway remains firmly committed to the two-state solution with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security. I thank you.

I thank the representative of Norway for that statement. I now give the floor to Muzna Ashria El Ajafi El-Ti, Charg d'affaires ad interim at the Permanent Observer Mission of the League of Arab States to the United Nations.

Thank you, Madam President, and congratulations on presidency over the Security Council this month and doing this with wisdom and responsibility.

Before I begin, I would like to thank Mr. Al-Akbarov for his comprehensive briefing. I would also like to align ourselves with the statement delivered by the permanent representative of Jordan in this regard. Madam President, allow me to deliver this statement before your august council on behalf of the Secretariat of the League of Arab States on the dangerous developments in the region and the need for a responsible international action to end the attacks, prevent the expansion of the conflict and maintain the sovereignty, security and territorial integrity of Arab countries. I quote, ladies and gentlemen, The Middle East is going through a dangerous phase where circles of confrontation are widening and crises are intertwining in a way that threatens regional and international peace and security. Current developments have reaffirmed that the security of the region is indivisible and that stability cannot be achieved with occupation, the use of force, the interference in the internal affairs of states or by turning their land, water or airspace into battlefields to settle scores. The Palestinian question, as it remains without a just and permanent solution, it remains the essence for the absence of security and stability in the region. There can be no peace with the Israeli occupation, with settlements, with annexation and displacement, there can be no stability as the Palestinian people are denied their right, their legitimate right to self-determination and establishment of an independent sovereign state with East Jerusalem as its capital. In the Gaza Strip, the urgent priority is to fully implement Security Council Resolution 2803, to end the attacks, to strengthen the ceasefire, and to guarantee the delivery of humanitarian assistance, and to move towards the second phase, including the full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and the beginning of recovery and reconstruction efforts. Obstructing the implementation of this resolution or implementing this resolution in a selective manner could undermine the calm and drag the region back to the circle of violence. The US administration holds a special responsibility in guaranteeing the implementation of the peace plan launched by President Trump last October, which was supported by the League of Arab States and the Security Council to lead to the reconstruction of Gaza and to open a political track to establish the Palestinian state based on the two-state solution. We must combat Israeli procrastination aimed at emptying the plan of its content to prolong the current situation as two million Palestinians continue to suffer, many of whom live in tents and lack food and basic educational and health services in the West Bank, including the occupied East Jerusalem settlements. and the confiscation of Palestinian property and land are ongoing in the absence of the effective implementation of resolution 2334, which undermines the two-state solution and imposes a de facto annexation. Attacks by settlers, including the killing of civilians, the burning of homes and places of worship, these reflect a systematic policy of forced displacement carried out unfortunately under the protection and encouragement of the occupation government. This requires urgent action from the Security Council to protect the Palestinian people. This protection is necessary to end the terror of settlers against unarmed civilians. Madam President, maintaining the security of the Middle East means we must address tensions based on respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries by supporting their national institutions, by rejecting occupation, division, and foreign interventions, by relying on political solutions and international law. In this regard, the League of Arab States strongly condemns Iranian attacks that targeted a number of Arab countries as a blatant violation of their sovereignty, of international law, of the principles of good neighborliness. We also condemn the targeting of commercial vessels and threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, in the Red Sea, and Bab-el-Mandeb Strait. These have dangerous repercussions on energy security, supply chains, food security and international economy. And we call for a safe passage through these corridors to end this suffocating crisis and to recover stability in the region, the League of Arab States call for a quick return to the understandings reached between the United States and Iran and a resumption of negotiations, a de-escalation, an end to attacks and violations, and a return to diplomacy while fully respecting international law and international legitimacy. No stability can be achieved with occupation, no security can be achieved as the sovereignty of countries is violated, and no future can be achieved if institutions are weakened or divided. We call on the Security Council to shoulder its responsibility and guarantee the full implementation of its resolutions without selectivity or delay, to protect unarmed civilians and maintain the sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries, and to support just and permanent political solutions. End of quote. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank Ms. Kitti for that statement. I now wish to give the floor to the representative of Japan.

Thank you, Madam President. Japan thanks the Democratic Republic of the Congo for creating this opportunity. Our immediate priority must be to de-escalate tensions and restore regional stability including by ensuring free and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Negotiations should continue with a view to addressing various issues, including the Iranian nuclear issue, one by one. Vessels should be able to transit the Strait without being subject to tolls or any other additional costs. There is no rationale or legitimacy in taking the global socioeconomy hostage by disrupting peaceful passage through the Strait, which has long served as a global public asset. Japan will continue to make every effort to foster an environment conducive to dialogue between the parties in close coordination with the international community. We welcome the trilateral framework agreed between Lebanon, Israel, and the United States, as a meaningful step toward lasting peace. We reiterate our call for the respect for Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity and the full implementation of the relevant Security Council resolutions, including Resolution 1701. Hamas's recent announcement regarding its preparations for the transfer of administrative responsibility to the National Committee for Administrative of Gaza, NCAG, and Israel's approval of the deployment of International Stabilization Force and NCSAG in Gaza are positive steps towards the operationalizing of the second phase of the comprehensive plan in line with the Security Council Resolution 2803. CCEPADD's approach is to leverage the resources and development expertise of East Asian countries to contribute to Palestinian state-building. Japan will continue to play a constructive role in advancing diplomatic efforts toward peace and stability in the Middle East. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Japan for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Spain.

Many thanks indeed, Madam President. Since the last open debate on the situation in the Middle East, the situation has worsened drastically. In view of that fact, the international community should assume its responsibility to change the course of a situation which, should it worsen, will threaten global stability on several fronts. In view of the open conflict in the Gulf, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the threat against Bab al-Mandab, in view of the humanitarian situation in Gaza and the violations committed by the occupation in the West Bank, in view of a situation that remains fragile in Lebanon, Syria and Iraq, our efforts today must unite to demand compliance with international law and IHL. There is no military solution to conflicts. We are fully committed to efforts at a multilateral level. As such, Spain defends diplomacy and dialogue as the only viable and effective path towards the resolution of conflicts. We support the laudable work done by regional mediators, many times are often under attack, and support the immediate cessation and permanent cessation of military operations on all fronts. It's only in working in that way that we'll forge a sustainable peace which endures over time, allowing in this connection to reaffirm the importance of the full and effective participation of women in negotiation processes. Respect for international law is the only way to resolve all unresolved questions with Iran, including the crisis around the Strait of Hormuz and the nuclear file. In light of the above, we express our grave concern at this new escalation of violence. We reiterate the fact that we condemn the indiscriminate and unjustified attacks by Iran against neighbouring states and we urge parties to cease all military operations. The arbitrary The military blockade of the Straits of Hormuz and the threats against Bab al-Mandab are an unacceptable violation of the freedom and safety of navigation. We reiterate the need to strengthen the Palestinian Authority. They are our vital partner and the only body with the legitimacy required to ensure the viability of a lasting sustainable peace and one which meets the aspirations of both the Palestinian and Israeli people. Turning to Gaza, we, before this Council, once again underscore the urgent need to implement resolution 2803. We condemn the expanded presence of the Israeli army in the Gaza Strip and we underscore the overriding need to act with urgency to palliate the humanitarian disaster besetting more than two million inhabitants in Gaza. We appeal to the Israeli government to allow the entry of humanitarian aid at scale and they must also protect the UN's work, including that of UNRWA, in the midst of the greatest financial crisis that has ever beset the United Nations system. 2026 Spain so far has already dispersed more than $15 million to Euro we wish to condemn the adoption of the law on the death penalty in Israel and the state of Palestine the terms of this law are discriminatory against the Palestinian people this discrimination is gravely alarming because it enshrines legal inequality between persons and lays waste to the most fundamental guarantees of due legal process on an issue which directly undermines the fundamental right to life it is a very it is attack an attack rather against the very principles of human dignity and equality. On the West Bank, we fervently condemn the hasty expansion of Israeli settlements and the continued proliferation of settlement outposts. At the same time, we're seeing a rising tide of violence which enjoys impunity, that is settler violence, and we're seeing arbitrary restrictions on Palestinian land access. We urge accountability for these violations. They threaten the viability of the Palestinian state. At the same time, they violate international law. Turning to Lebanon, we recognise and support the brave decisions taken by the Lebanese Government in defence of the full respect for its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. We reiterate our commitment to the full implementation of resolution 1701. We reiterate our firm support for the Lebanese people and Lebanese institutions. We will continue to support efforts to forge a lasting stability. We fully support the strengthening of the Lebanese Armed Forces bilaterally and together with our European partners. Our work here is to ensure that the LAF can consolidate control across the full extent of Lebanese territory. Here we welcome the signing of a trilateral agreement between Lebanon, Israel and the US on the 26th of June in Washington. This should stand as a first step towards a comprehensive and just peace in accordance with the previously outlined principles. We unwaveringly support the work of UNIFIL. We have been present in that mission for 20 years with a sizeable contingent. We recognize the fundamental role played by the blue helmets. We condemn the unacceptable attacks against mission personnel and we express our sincere condolences following recent events. A comprehensive investigation into these deaths must be conducted and all such attacks are a violation of international law. We welcome the options presented by the Secretary-General for the implementation of 1701 once UNIFIL's mandate concludes. We will continue working actively with TCCs and PCCs and Security Council members to guarantee an orderly transition and to contribute to efforts underway to ensure stability down the blue line following UNIFIL's withdrawal. On Syria, we stand at a critical juncture for the country and its people. Together with the challenge of rebuilding and buttressing legitimate and democratic institutions after decades of conflict, concerns remain alongside internal and external pressure. There's also a serious humanitarian crisis and there is a complex geopolitical situation at play at a regional level with security concerns also. We support a peaceful and inclusive political transition process, one which guarantees the full respect for the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, and we will continue working with the transitional government of Syria in this regard. I wish to underscore that the regional context in the Middle East is today a devastating one. We cannot turn away from it or let us be distracted by other issues. The Security Council must act and must do so urgently. Member States of the United Nations have a responsibility and indeed the moral obligation to use all means at our disposal to achieve the restoration of peace and stability in the Middle East. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Spain for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Madam President, despite the declared ceasefire, Gaza remains devastated and under siege. Israel, the occupying regime, continues to violate the ceasefire through ongoing military attacks and severe restriction on humanitarian access. It is further deepening the suffering of civilians. At the same time, the Israeli regime continues its illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. in clear violation of international law and relevant United Nations resolutions. Israel's repeated acts of aggression against Lebanon and continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity further threaten regional peace and security. The continued unlawful actions of the Israeli regime pose a grave threat to international peace and security. Against this backdrop, Iran reiterates that any credible solution must ensure a permanent ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, the full withdrawal of Israeli occupying forces, and full UN membership for the state of Palestine. Humanitarian assistance and Gaza's reconstruction must never be conditioned on political or military objectives. accountability is indispensable the Israeli regime together with those that enable this regime for its atrocious crimes through political military and economic support must be held responsible for grave violations of international humanitarian law the issuance of arrest warrants by the ICC on 21st November 2024 against the criminal Prime Minister of the Israeli regime for the commission of war crimes and crimes against humanity is a clear reminder that no one is above international law. The representative of the United States has once again resorted to lies, disinformation, and a campaign of distortion in a desperate attempt to justify the United States' unlawful acts of aggression against Iran. These allegations are part of the long-standing hostile policy pursued by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran to advance their political and military objectives, conceal their unlawful actions and malicious activities in the region, and justify the U.S. destabilizing military presence in the region. However, the facts are clear and cannot be denied. The United States is the aggressor. Through its acts of aggression against Iran, the United States has violated the Charter of the United Nations and fundamental principles of international law, including the pre-emptory prohibition on the use of force and the prohibition of aggression. By deliberately targeting civilian and civilian infrastructure, including schools, hospitals, medical facilities, bridges, sport facilities, and other essential infrastructure, the United States has committed grave violations of international humanitarian law, including war crimes. The attacks on the Minab school is a tragic and undeniable example of those crimes. The President of the United States and other senior officials have openly acknowledged the commission of these heinous crimes and have even expressed pride in them. Such statements constitute further evidence of their responsibility. The United States bears full international responsibility for its internationally wrongful acts. Those who are responsible for these grave crimes will sooner or later face accountability before competent international judicial bodies. No one is above international law and there will be no impunity. The international community and the Security Council must not allow these crimes to be normalized. Silence and impunity will only encourage their repetition. Madam President, in conclusion, we reiterate that all Iran's measures are defensive, necessary, and consistent with international law. The root causes of the current situation are clear. United States ongoing unlawful actions pose a serious threat to regional stability, freedom of navigation, and the security of the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. The Islamic Republic of Iran has exercised and will continue to exercise its inherent right of self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. to protect its people and to defend and safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and vital national interests against US acts of aggression. I thank the representative of the Islamic Republic of Iran for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Poland.

Thank you, Madam President. I would like to thank the Democratic Republic of the Congo for convening this timely debate on the situation in the Middle East. Madam President, we are deeply concerned with the recent escalation of the situation in the Persian Gulf. Once again, the current events demonstrate that energy security and freedom of navigation must remain central to the resolution of the conflict and regional peace solution. In that context, we are concerned with the Houthis' ability to threaten the fragile balance of maritime traffic in the Red Sea. With that in mind, we note with interest that the decision taken by the countries in the region to develop alternative strategic transport and energy corridors, including oil and gas pipelines, as well as railway networks, in anticipation that the long-term operation of the Strait of Hormuz will remain subject to the periodic disruptions. We remain equally concerned by the growing use of disinformation and the continued targeting of civilian infrastructure, trends that have come to define contemporary conflicts from the Middle East to Ukraine. Madam President, this state of no peace, no war cannot endure indefinitely. Geography cannot change, but political choices can. And meaningful dialogue remains the only path to lasting resolution. Poland commends the efforts of all mediators and remains firmly committed to supporting diplomatic de-escalation. Two issues remain central, the full opening of the Strait of Hormuz and control over Iran's nuclear program, requiring full Iranian cooperation with the IAEA and compliance with the NPT and the Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement. Let me repeat, nuclear safety, maritime security and freedom of navigation remain essential to international stability. Madam President, Recognition of the Palestinian people's aspiration for statehood and support for the two-state solution remain key elements of Poland's Middle East policy, consistently reflected in our voting at the UN and grounded in the New York Declaration of September 2005. In this context, Poland shares the international community's alarm over escalating tensions in the West Bank. We urge Israel to protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and hold perpetrators accountable. We also oppose death penalty in all circumstances and called on Israel to maintain its moratorium on executions. Poland remains gravely concerned by the actions targeting UNRWA, whose work is indispensable for millions of refugees. More broadly, Madam President, let me underline that the protection of civilians remain a matter of the highest importance for Poland. We call for full respect for international humanitarian law and for holding accountable all those responsible for its violation, including attacks on humanitarian personnel. This issue carries particular weight for us. In April 2024, a Polish citizen was among the World Central Kitchen volunteers killed in that attack in Gaza. We once again demand an immediate and full end to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure and safe unhindered humanitarian access everywhere, whether in the Middle East, in Africa, or in Ukraine. Madam President, our commitment extends beyond words. Before I conclude, allow me to highlight Poland's humanitarian and development support for the region. Poland actively supports humanitarian projects through Polish aid, NGOs and various UN agencies, with particular focus on initiatives implemented in Lebanon, Palestine and Syria. Our priorities include strengthening local resilience by ensuring access to healthcare, mostly through mobile clinics, supporting local entrepreneurship, reinforcing local administration and civil defence, enhancing preparedness and response to natural disasters, and expanding access to renewable energy. Our commitment to the people of this region remains steadfast. And I thank you.
I thank the representative of Poland for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Bulgaria.

Thank you, Madam President. Bulgaria remains deeply concerned by the continuing instability across the Middle East. any serious implications for regional and international peace and security. In this regard, Bulgaria expresses its strong support for the efforts of High Representative Nikolay Mladenov and the Board of Peace toward the implementation of the comprehensive plan and Security Council Resolution 2803. We welcome the Office's efforts to support the implementation of the ceasefire arrangement, facilitate effective governance, advance recovery and reconstruction in Gaza and coordinate international efforts in support of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict. Strengthening this mechanism remains essential to translating political commitment into tangible results on the ground. We underline the importance of the permanent disarmament of Hamas and no other non-state armed groups. Hamas cannot be part of the future governance of Gaza. We join the call for immediate, safe and unimpeded access and sustained distribution of humanitarian assistance at scale into and throughout Gaza. The deterioration of the situation in the West Bank, including the increase in settler violence and settlement activities, is a source of serious concern and needs to be addressed. Bulgaria remains committed to a comprehensive, just and lasting peace based on a two-state solution in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, whereby two democratic states, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders. On Lebanon, we welcome the trilateral framework agreement signed by Lebanon, Israel, and the United States in Washington on 26th of June. which offers an important opportunity to advance de-escalation, restore Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and move towards more sustainable security arrangements. The situation in Lebanon nevertheless remains fragile. The full disarmament of Hezbollah and other non-state armed groups remain essential for lasting peace and security. Bulgaria reaffirms its support for Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as for the efforts of the Lebanese authorities to strengthen the Lebanese armed forces and extend state authority throughout the whole Lebanese territory. The implementation of Security Council Resolution 1701 in its entirety continued to be of key importance. With regard to Syria, Bulgaria remains fully committed to supporting a peaceful and inclusive Syrian-led and Syrian-owned transition that upholds human rights and guarantees the participation of all Syrians without distinction. For this transition to succeed, Syria must be insulated from regional hostilities. We call on all external actors to fully respect Syria's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. On Iran, we express cautious hope that the halt in military strikes will create a new window for a ceasefire that could pave the way for the resumption of diplomatic engagement with the aim of reopening the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with international law and ultimately reaching a negotiated solution to the outstanding issues related to Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programs. Bulgaria is concerned that the periodic resumption of military escalation between the United States and Iran increases the unpredictability of the situation and the risk of miscalculation and calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint. We condemn the unilateral attacks of Iran against countries in the region, as well as the disruption of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz. We underline the need to fully ensure freedom of navigation, as well as free and safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, as reflected in UNCLOS. We also underline the importance of safeguarding maritime routes and freedom of navigation throughout the wider region, including the Red Sea and the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait. The recent threats by the Houthis are unacceptable and must be categorically rejected. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the representative of Bulgaria for this statement. I now give the floor to the representative of the United Arab Emirates.

Sayeda Raeesa.

First, progress must be made towards the full implementation of Security Council Resolution 2803, including consolidating the ceasefire in the Gaza Strip, ensuring Hamas's disarmament, creating the conditions necessary for the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza to begin its work, and expediting the deployment of the International Stabilization Force. but also through a full Israeli withdrawal from the Gaza Strip and enabling the Palestinian Authority, after the necessary reform, to assume its full responsibilities in both Gaza and the West Bank. We continue to provide humanitarian assistance, in particular through Operation Chivalrous Night III, alongside other initiatives. such as projects to combat rodents and pests to reduce epidemic risks, but also by organizing collective weddings and taking care of excellent students. And we do this in partnership with the United Nations. These efforts should proceed in parallel with initiatives aimed at advancing the two-state solution, independent and sovereign Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as capital, living side by side with Israel in peace and security.
I thank the UAE for the statement. I now give the floor to Malaysia.

Madam President, Malaysia thanks the Democratic Republic of the Congo for convening this quarterly open debate. We also thank Mr. Alagbaroff for his comprehensive briefing. I thank the representative of Malaysia for this statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Tunisia.

Thank you, Madam President. At the outset, I would like to thank the Democratic Republic of the Congo for convening this meeting. We would like to express our support to you as you discharge your functions presiding over the Council. As we've already said on many occasions, the tragic situation in the Middle East is a direct result of the failure of international community to restore its inalienable rights to the Palestinian people throughout their territory. We call on the international community to address the violations committed by the occupying power, and to assume their political and moral responsibility in the maintenance of international peace and security in order to assure the enforcement of international law, in particular international humanitarian law. We reaffirm our support to the vital role played by UNRWA in providing relief for Palestinian refugees and its outstanding contribution to regional stability. The international community has to continue providing political and financial support to UNRWA and reject any attempts to distract, to detract from their mandate. We support our Palestinian brothers in their self-determination. their struggle for the full restoration of their rights and the establishment of their state on the entire territory of Palestine with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
I thank Tunisia for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Portugal.

Thank you, Madam President. Starting with the Gulf, Portugal calls for the full implementation of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. We urge all relevant parties to uphold international law, including international humanitarian law and freedom of navigation. Portugal supports a diplomatic solution as the only viable path to a comprehensive and long-lasting peace. The same applies to Yemen. Turning to Lebanon, we welcome the trilateral framework agreement and highlight the importance of its implementation in the context of existing UN Security Council resolutions, including 1701. We believe the UN should continue to have a role post UNIFIL. Concerning Syria, Portugal welcomes the inaugural session of the People's Assembly and the recent visit by the Secretary General of the United Nations, both of which mark significant milestones in the country's political transition. Regarding Palestine, the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains grievous. Portugal calls for the full implementation of the comprehensive plan. We stress that the UN and all its agencies, including UNRWA, as well as international NGOs must be able to fulfill their roles. Violations of the ceasefire must stop. Furthermore, the Palestinian Authority should be involved in preparation for its return to the Strip. In the West Bank and East Jerusalem, Portugal is concerned by the surge in settlers violence and Israel unilateral actions aimed at increasing its control over the occupied Palestinian territory. including the expanding settlements which are illegal under international law. This is the spirit that will guide us as we will serve as elected members of the Security Council in 27 and 28. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Portugal for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Canada.

Madam President, Canada remains deeply concerned by the ongoing conflict with Iran. We reiterate the need to work towards a diplomatic resolution to the conflict and support efforts by Pakistan and Qatar and other regional partners towards the resumption of negotiations. Canada urges all parties to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. We condemn in the strongest terms Iran's strikes against Gulf states, Jordan, and other partners in the region. We stand firmly in support of our Gulf partners' sovereignty and security and commend their ongoing efforts towards dialogue and de-escalation. Canada will continue to pressure Iran to end its malign behaviour. To this end, we have imposed sanctions on a total of 227 Iranian individuals and 260 entities. These sanctions address concerns related to Iran's abhorrent human rights abuses, nuclear program, its funding of proxy terrorist groups, and the transfer of UAV and drone technology to malign actors. Canada is equally concerned by the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, where the continued disruption of maritime security poses a serious threat to our economies and overall security, including critical supply chains. Canada calls on Iran to respect navigation rights and safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz in line with international law. Canada is working with partners towards restoring maritime security and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and we stand ready to support proposed French and UK initiatives. We are also concerned by the recent Houthi threats against Saudi Arabia, including to disrupt the lawful passage of vessels in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait. The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait must remain open and safe for international navigation, free from attacks or interference in accordance with international law. Canada welcomes initial steps taken under the Trilateral Framework Agreement, including the recent deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces in areas of southern Lebanon, and encourages the continued implementation of commitments by all parties. We reiterate the importance of full respect for Lebanon's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the commitments undertaken by all parties in accordance with international law and relevant UN Security Council resolutions, including 1701. We also welcome efforts by the Lebanese authorities to extend state authority throughout Lebanese territory and encourage continued progress on the reforms necessary to support Lebanon's long-term stability and recovery. Canada remains concerned by ongoing security incidents affecting civilians and civilian infrastructure and by the threats to the safety and security of UNIFIL personnel. We underscore that peacekeepers must be able to carry out their mandated tasks safely and without interference.

We should not lose sight of the immense suffering of civilians in Gaza or the humanitarian crisis which continues despite the ceasefire. We in Canada have committed themselves to provide more than $500 million in international assistance this 2023 and we reiterate our appeal for a greater humanitarian access. We condemn terrorist attacks by Hamas in Israel on the 7th of October, 2023, which took the life of about 1,200 people, including Canadians. The political negotiations should lead to Hamas disarmament and its withdrawal from the governance of Gaza. We welcome and support the progress realized by the Palestinian Authority in implementing their reform program, including the local elections in April and the announcement of legislative elections in November this year. In the West Bank, the expansion of settlements continues unabated. Canada asks once again that the settlement policy by Israel be rescinded immediately, including the E1 project. It compromises the prospects for a two-state solution. We also urge Israel to prevent violence committed by extremist settlers and to take the perpetrators to justice. We have imposed five rounds of sanctions against 19 people and 12 entities connected to this violence and will continue looking at any measures which are appropriate to tackle this issue. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Canada for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Iceland.

Thank you, Madam President. Eight months ago, this Council adopted resolution 2803 endorsing the 20-point comprehensive plan to end the conflict in Gaza. and the role of the Board of Peace in its implementation. Since then, some of the plan's key objectives have been achieved. All living hostages were released and the remains of those killed have been returned to their families. A ceasefire has been in effect, although an imperfect one, and humanitarian assistance resumed with some improvements in the rate of delivery. Nonetheless, the humanitarian situation remains critical and humanitarian access restricted, for many essential items. Regrettably, Israel has continued to delay, obstruct and prevent the work of UN agencies, including UNRWA, and key international non-governmental organizations in Gaza. Meanwhile, Israel, by its own account, has expanded its control of Gaza instead of gradually withdrawing in accordance with the comprehensive peace plan. Madam President, The full promise of resolution 2803 remains unrealized, and we call for more progress towards the peace and relief it pledged for Palestinians in Gaza. More needs to be done to support the Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza in carrying out its work and all efforts made for urgent deployment of the vetted Palestinian police and the international stabilization force in line with resolution 2803. We reiterate that Hamas has no role in the future of Palestine and that militant factions in Gaza must be decommissioned. Their defiance must neither be tolerated nor be permitted to prevent the implementation of the peace plan. Iceland is gravely concerned by the situation in the West Bank, which continues to deteriorate with ongoing settlement expansion in violation of international law. There have been serious incidents of violence in recent weeks, as we heard from Mr. Alakbarov's briefing this morning. Regrettably, settler violence and crimes persist with impunity and are fueled and enabled by inflammatory rhetoric and permissive government policy. While it may almost seem futile in the current dire circumstances to call for a two-state solution, where Israelis and Palestinians live side by side in peace and mutual recognition, It remains the only viable path to sustainable peace and security. The recent report of the Under-Secretary-General for emphasizes the fact that even after the ceasefire, the Palestinian people continue to face incredibly difficult conditions, new deaths, mass displacement, and confinement to ever-shrinking strips of land with very limited access to essential services. Legal and political equality are the linchpin of a genuine and sustainable peace. It also requires that all are held accountable on the basis of obligations under international law. Equality is not a privilege, it is a vital prerequisite to resolve conflict which has already raged on for too many decades. Madam President, there can be no lasting peace while occupation, annexation and the very negotiation of fundamental rights continue. Peace demands respect for human dignity, respect for international law, for international humanitarian law and for the right of peoples to self-determination. These principles are not abstract concepts, rather they are the very foundation of any viable and sustainable political solution. In accordance with the aforementioned the group of friends reiterates its commitment to continue working to ensure the full exercise of the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people including their right to an independent sovereign state there can be no peace in the Middle East without a just comprehensive and lasting solution to the Palestinian question a solution rooted in international law and the relevant resolutions of this organization we appeal for the establishment of a sovereign viable Palestinian state on the basis of pre-1967 lines with Jerusalem as its capital in accordance with international law, the relevant resolutions of the United Nations and the two-state solution. Here we must guarantee the right of return of Palestinian refugees in accordance with relevant UN resolution. Allow me now, in my national capacity, to add a number of brief comments. The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, faithful to the very tenets of its diplomacy of peace, reiterates its appeal for dialogue and restraint with a view to achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting solution to the Palestinian question. Lanka. Madam President, at the outset, Sri Lanka welcomes the Democratic Republic of the Congo's presidency of the Security Council and appreciates the convening of this important meeting.
